text: {"claims": [{"context": "upon DNA damage, in general", "effect": "activates", "evidence_quote": "The tumor suppressor p53 is a transcription factor that, upon DNA damage, is activated to induce sequence-specific target genes involved in either cancer cell growth arrest or apoptosis [112].", "location": "Oncosuppressor p53 and apoptosis", "source": "DNA damage", "target": "p53"}, {"context": "in response to genotoxic stress", "effect": "activates", "evidence_quote": "in response to genotoxic stress, however, p53 undergoes post-translational modifications that allow the protein to escape MDM2 control, accumulate, and become active [133].", "location": "Waking up the guardian: p53 as a druggable target", "source": "genotoxic stress", "target": "p53"}, {"context": "in response to UV irradiation and chemotherapy", "effect": "activates", "evidence_quote": "a key determinant in shifting the p53 pro-apoptotic transcription in response, for instance, to UV irradiation and chemotherapy [136,137].", "location": "Waking up the guardian: p53 as a druggable target", "source": "UV irradiation", "target": "p53"}, {"context": "in response to low genotoxic damage", "effect": "inhibits", "evidence_quote": "MDM2 can also trigger, in response to low genotoxic damage, the downregulation of p53 apoptotic activator HIPK2 [148].", "location": "Waking up the guardian: p53 as a druggable target", "source": "low genotoxic damage", "target": "HIPK2"}]}
